title: Release binaries for desktop-ish Linux: how? AppImage/Flatpak/something else?

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body:
Uh, to be clear, this project does “support” Linux, in the sense that you can build it for Linux, it's just not something we promise will be easy or work well, for the time being at least.

There was an existing discussion about Linux support in https://github.com/hikari-no-yume/touchHLE/issues/3.

I don't really want to do Linux binary releases, it's not a single platform in the way that Windows or macOS are. But I am willing to make it easier to build yourself on Linux.

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body: Also, if you hit any problems while building it yourself, please tell us about them (probably in the thread I linked).

comments.author: WingofaGriffin
comments.body:
I want to revive this discussion a bit.

It seems that the biggest objection to Linux binaries being released is due to all the different distros and dependencies that differ. I would argue that Flatpak and AppImage seek to solve that issue directly, by specifically being distro agnostic.

Literally from the [AppImage front page](https://appimage.org):
> "As a user, I want to download an application from the original author, and run it on my Linux desktop system just like I would do with a Windows or Mac application."
>"As an application author, I want to provide packages for Linux desktop systems, without the need to get it 'into' a distribution and without having to build for gazillions of different distributions."

These two package types bundle the deps in with the binary (a bit more complicated than that, but you get the jist). When paired with a CI tool like GitHub actions, which you already seem to be using, it should be pretty easy to automate a new set of builds, especially with the GitHub provided Ubuntu instance.

Let me know if you want to discuss further, I appriciate the existing Linux support you do have, and have given, but want to see if we can make this easier for all of us :)

Ah, thanks for the heads up.

Unrelated: I wonder if I can avoid using any of these imaging formats. I've refused to have “Linux” builds because it doesn't seem like a well-defined platform to me, but actually, touchHLE probably only needs glibc, SDL 2, and maybe a handful of other things. That's a small enough surface area that I think imaging/containerisation/etc is superfluous. I should do some experiments.

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body:
Having read a bit of the AppImage documentation I'm not really convinced of the quality of that particular system. Since an AppImage is just an executable anyway, maybe we could just ship a static build of touchHLE if people really want that. Flatpak looks better-designed, though the particular way it handles GPU drivers is quite unfortunate.

To be honest, though, I don't really want to maintain Linux packaging, and I question what the actual benefit to users would be. touchHLE works well in WINE and I can recommend running it that way.

comments.author: Samueru-sama
comments.body:
> Having read a bit of the AppImage documentation I'm not really convinced of the quality of that particular system.

Read this instead: https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/blob/main/HOW-TO-MAKE-THESE.md

The AppImage documentation is abandoned and says a lot of things that are not true anymore, it does not even make mention of [Go-appimage](https://github.com/probonopd/go-appimage) which works similar to sharun.

See also https://github.com/AppImage/docs.appimage.org/pull/102

EDIT: This specific AppImage even uses a runtime [that does not need FUSE at all](https://github.com/VHSgunzo/uruntime) to work

>maybe we could just ship a static build of touchHLE if people really want that. 

Sure, if you can make a fully static binary that works better than AppImage, however that means: 

* You will have to link mesa statically (in this AppImage I ship a smaller version that makes the final AppImage **less than 30 MiB**). 

* You will not have hardware acceleration with nvidia, because the proprietary nvidia driver is massive and cannot be bundled due to its license.

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body: The whole concept of bundling your own graphics driver (Mesa in this case) into a Flatpak runtime or AppImage is absurd to me. This is why people don't take Linux seriously! Every 3D graphics API is designed with a stable ABI for dynamic linking, so that you aren't locked into a particular vendor for your hardware or drivers. Why would you sacrifice that willingly… it's a great way to ensure that the app won't work with next year's hardware.

comments.author: Samueru-sama
comments.body:
> so that you aren't locked into a particular vendor for your hardware or drivers.

>  it's a great way to ensure that the app won't work with next year's hardware.

**You are not locked into a specific version with sharun!** You also don't need to include mesa drivers either, however that means that hardware acceleration is broken in non-glibc systems. 

I used to not ship mesa, but then got these issues: 

* https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/mpv-AppImage/issues/19

* https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Citron-AppImage/issues/14

So now using the host mesa is locked behind an env variable in sharun.

By default with `aarch64` we still allow using the host mesa drivers, because those often have vendor specific patches that have not been upstreamed. 

**EDIT:** [Also with nvidia we always use the nvidia driver of the host.](https://github.com/pkgforge-dev/Anylinux-AppImages/blob/main/HOW-TO-MAKE-THESE.md#what-about-nvidia)
